en: Solid ice in the Cordillera mountains melts into liquid water when the sun's heat increases its temperature.
Iron gates in humid coastal towns undergo a chemical change to form reddish-brown rust when exposed to oxygen and moisture.
Evaporating seawater in salt farms like those in Dasmarinas leaves behind solid salt crystals, separating the mixture.
Liquid lava from Mayon Volcano cools and solidifies into hard, black igneous rock through a physical change.
Pumice rocks ejected from volcanoes float on ocean water because their density is lower than that of liquid water.
Fallen banana leaves in a compost pit undergo chemical changes as microbes break them down into dark, nutrient-rich soil.
Floodwaters in the Pasig River form a heterogeneous mixture where solid soil particles are temporarily suspended in liquid water.
Invisible water vapor in the cool morning air condenses into liquid dew drops on the leaves of a sampaguita plant.
Black volcanic sand in Camiguin contains magnetite, a magnetic material that sticks to a magnet when separated from the mixture.
Fresh coconut milk left under the hot tropical sun undergoes a chemical change, souring and separating into solid curds and liquid.
Stirring solid brown sugar into liquid calamansi juice causes a physical change where the sugar dissolves to form a sweet solution.
Solid naphthalene mothballs stored in local wooden cabinets slowly sublimate, turning directly into a gas to repel fabric-eating insects.
